raw_response:
Aiya, another year. Let me think through what I'm doing on each plot. Just me and the old lady at home now, and these old bones don't bend like they used to. Five mu is plenty for two of us — I'm not taking on more.

**The vegetable plot (about 2 mu)** — this is my rotation land, good soil, close to the well. Cabbage in spring like always, then longbean over the summer when the cabbage comes out, then spinach in the fall. This rotation works — the longbean puts something back in the soil so the spinach doesn't need much fertilizer after. I learned this from doing it year after year.

**Chili (1 mu)** — separate plot near the road so I can pick easy. Chili is fussy and needs water, but the price at the market is decent if I time the picks right. I'll transplant after Qingming when the cold snap is past — last year I rushed and lost half my seedlings to a late frost, won't do that again.

**Maize (2 mu)** — this is my easy crop, mostly for ourselves and to sell a little. I plant it after the wheat would come out if I had wheat — middle of June. Doesn't need much fussing. The extension fellow said I should use 18 kg N per mu but I usually do about 15, that's enough for what I get out of this land.

**On fertilizer generally** — I buy a few bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) and some urea at the township agri shop in early spring, that's my main outlay. For the vegetables I also throw on whatever chicken manure I can get from my nephew who keeps layers — costs me almost nothing and the cabbage loves it.

**Water** — well water is metered now, costs me real money. I water when the crop needs it, not on a schedule. Vegetables drink more than maize, that's just how it is.

**Pesticide** — cabbage worm is the worst, I have to spray two or three times for that. Chili gets aphids. Maize I usually don't bother spraying. I buy what the shop owner recommends, he knows what's going around.

**Labor** — just us two. Can't afford hired hands except maybe a day or two at chili harvest if it's coming on heavy. The kids are in the city, they don't come back for farm work anymore.
